claim: *The Delegation Staircase.* As explicit representation and environmental enforcement accumulated, larger units of engineering work could be delegated. Representation moved system knowledge out of one person's head; enforcement moved repeatable admission decisions out of direct review. Human work moved from reading every diff toward system-level strategy and the residual semantic judgment the environment could not yet decide. A failure in either representation or enforcement could move work back down the staircase.
topology: Five ascending stages with a common right edge, growing environment region at left and a nonzero taper beside the human-focus column.

alt: Five white stage cards rise from Co-coder through QA, Review lead, Tech lead and Architect. Each names the delegated work and the engineering environment, with a short italic explanation. A pale stepped region at left grows toward the upper stages, representing accumulating representations and enforcement. Outside the cards, a black taper narrows from the bottom stage to a nonzero width at the top; aligned bold labels describe the remaining human work: reading every diff and admitting changes; adjudicating findings; residual semantic review; system map and strategy; residual semantics and strategy. The trajectories are qualitative. Failure in representation or enforcement can move work down.
